subject.title: Plugin `message_sending` hooks silently bypassed on channel agent-reply delivery paths (2026.5.26, still present in 2026.6.1)

question: Which open branch should be treated as the canonical fix for the `message_sending` safety-hook boundary across configured dispatcher delivery and Telegram streamed-final replies?
rationale: The code path is a documented pre-send rewrite/cancel boundary used by safety plugins, and the available fixes make different ownership choices that automation should not settle without maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt the broader exactly-once branch
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/93216 as the canonical path after resolving its current review blocker, rebase/conflict state, and proof gap.

options.title: Land a narrow dispatcher repair first
options.body: Pick a smaller dispatcher-only branch if maintainers intentionally defer Telegram streamed-final gating and track that remainder separately.

options.title: Pause all overlapping branches
options.body: Hold the open PRs until a maintainer specifies the permanent dispatcher-vs-delivery hook ownership contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt the broader exactly-once branch
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/93216 as the canonical path after resolving its current review blocker, rebase/conflict state, and proof gap.

likelyOwner.reason: The core decision is in the dispatcher hook-composition surface introduced by `reply_payload_sending`, with Telegram follow-through from the linked candidate branch.
